design:
Tier 2: an autonomous agent changing git state on the operator's work without review, a migration, a cross-cutting hook in the scheduler. Rollback: the doctor is off by default and per project; disabling it leaves stall records as an inert table.
D1. A stall is a row (migration): project, key (cause + subject, e.g. delivery_refused:task-x), cause, text, first_seen, doctor_run_id, outcome. Recorded where each signal is already decided: decide_firing's stalled/refused results, the integration writer, _emit_review_unstaffed, run reconciliation, plus one periodic no-progress sweep in the existing scheduler (not a new process).
D2. The doctor is the first manager entry that is an agent run, not a one-shot: a JobSpec with needs_runner and a new 'agent' flag. It runs under a reserved Hub-owned agent identity per project (name chosen to pass AGENT_NAME_RE and checked against existing agents, never added to RESERVED_AGENT_NAMES), so turn_scheduler, budgets, traces and ask_user all apply unchanged. This revises manager.py's 'not an agent' rule for this one entry; say so in that docstring.
D3. Autonomy is enforced by the tools, not only the prompt: the doctor's tool set adds the unblock actions of FR unblock-without-review as Hub routes that refuse anything in ask-before-hardcore unless a matching answered question id is passed. The prompt explains; the routes guarantee.
D4. Its merges skip review by being Hub-performed integrations of doctor commits, gated on project checks, recorded with actor 'doctor'.
D5. Needs you: a doctor question is an ordinary Question with blocking=true, so the existing Overview list shows it (OverviewScreen.tsx:78-111); the stall row also gets a Needs-you entry until resolved, which closes the gap that stalled loops never appear there.

open_questions.question: The doctor's agent name (must pass AGENT_NAME_RE and not collide with an existing agent): 'doctor', or something in the brand's voice?
Default no-progress window (30 min proposed) and per-stall turn cap (proposed 40 turns)?

problem: Night of 2026-10-22, the operator's real Hub, project AgentWeave, loop job-4d32116a1530 ('Pull the thread'): three approved tasks never merged because the shared checkout had another process's uncommitted tracked files (four task_integrations rows 'skipped', 00:20-00:27 UTC). The next task, task-d4732f356636, needed two of those unmerged branches stacked, and they conflicted in hub/hub/project_thread.py; at 00:35 its delivery was refused with 'No firing will retry it. Fix it, then withdraw that input'. Nothing acted on it until the operator woke. Every signal involved already exists (scheduler.py:2375 _loop_stall_reason, the delivery refusal, task_integrations status, review_unstaffed at scheduler.py:3025, agent_status.py stale heartbeats) but all are passive: none reaches Overview -> Needs you, and none tries a repair. Manager jobs cannot help as they are: each is a one-shot spawn with no tools and no ask_user (manager.py:9-13).

requirements.rationale: Last night's stall had a named cause the Hub already computed; the catch-all covers the stall nobody has named yet (operator: 'any stall').
requirements.statement: The Hub MUST record a stall, keyed by project and cause, when a loop firing is refused or decided stalled, when an approved task's integration is skipped or fails, when a completed task has no permitted reviewer, when a run's heartbeat goes stale mid-turn or a task is in_progress with no live run, and when a project with an enabled loop and open work has made no progress (no run started, no task transition) for a configurable time, 30 minutes by default.

requirements.rationale: A five-minute loop would otherwise spawn a doctor every firing.
requirements.statement: The doctor MUST be woken at most once per distinct stall key; a loop that keeps stalling on the same cause MUST NOT wake it again, and a stall with a new cause MUST.

requirements.rationale: Repairs need tools and ask_user, which a one-shot manager spawn has not got; the brief starts it from evidence.
requirements.statement: With the doctor enabled for the project, a recorded stall MUST start a doctor run on the configured runner and model, in its own worktree and its own conversation, whose first turn carries a Hub-written brief: the stall's cause and text, the loop, the task and its dependency chain, the latest integration rows, and the project checkout's git status.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-23: full autonomy to unblock, its changes do not go through QA.
requirements.statement: The doctor MUST be able, without asking and without QA review, to resolve merge conflicts on task branches, rebuild a task's branch, retry a skipped or failed integration, withdraw a refused input and re-brief the task's agent, restart a dead run, hand an unstaffed task to a free agent, and reset a stuck task's status; before merging a commit of its own it MUST run the project's configured checks, and a failing check MUST turn the fix into a question.

requirements.rationale: Operator: 'ask the user about more hardcore changes'. Last night's first cause was another process's files, which only the operator may decide about.
requirements.statement: The doctor MUST ask the operator through ask_user, and MUST NOT act until answered, before touching uncommitted changes it did not make, rewriting or reverting main or deleting a branch or work, rejecting or deleting a task, changing a specification or its requirements, changing agents, permissions, budgets or project settings, or changing product logic beyond the conflicting hunks; the question MUST appear under Overview -> Needs you and the stalled loop MUST stay paused until it is answered.

requirements.rationale: Unreviewed changes need a readable trail; an unbounded doctor is a new stall.
requirements.statement: Each doctor run MUST end recorded as fixed, asked, or gave up, with what it did, on the stall's record and in its conversation; its turns MUST count against the project's budget and stop at a per-stall turn cap.

in_scope: Recording a stall, keyed by its cause, from the named signals and a no-progress catch-all
A 'doctor' manager entry (enabled, runner, model) on the Manager page, off by default
The doctor as a real agent run: its own conversation, its own worktree, MCP tools including ask_user, costed and budgeted like any run
A Hub-written brief of the stall's facts handed to the doctor's first turn
The doctor's outcome (fixed, asked, gave up) recorded and shown
non_goals: Feature work: the doctor only unblocks agents; once the loop moves, its run ends
Inferring stalls from agent prose (the retired detector, migration 0082, stays retired)
A per-agent poller or a second runtime: the Hub records stalls where it already decides them
OS or push notifications: escalation is Needs you in the app
Repairing the shared-checkout setup itself (two automations in one working tree)

summary: When a project's work stalls (a loop firing refused or stalled, approved work that never merged, a task nobody may review, a dead run, or simply no progress), the Hub records the stall once and wakes a doctor: a manager-configured agent run that reads the cause, unblocks the agents on its own where the fix is mechanical, and asks the operator through Needs you before anything hardcore.
